title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (section 8 of the notes). X is a smooth projective connected variety of dimension n over a perfect field k of characteristic p>0, embedded in P^r. Y is a smooth hyperplane section, or a hypersurface section of degree d, of dimension n-1. E(Y) = Coker(H^{n-1}_cris(X) -> H^{n-1}_cris(Y)) is the crystalline 'vanishing cohomology'. On the previous page, an exact sequence (8.1.3) compares E(Y)⊗_W k with the de Rham vanishing cohomology E_DR(Y). It does so through kernels and cokernels of maps u_0, u_1, u_2 coming from universal coefficients, Poincaré duality and weak Lefschetz, all with torsion kept.

Every term carries a functorial p-linear Frobenius. Grothendieck then applies the exact functor V -> V_ss: the largest subspace on which F is bijective, equivalently the stable or unit-root part, with F nilpotent on the quotient.

On this page:
(1) Semisimple p-linear spaces form a category equivalent to finite-dimensional F_p-representations of G = Gal(k̄/k). This is Lang's theorem / Artin–Schreier: V_ss = (V⊗k̄)^{F=1} ⊗ k. This category has a self-duality. Under it, (Coker u_2)_ss and (Ker u_2)_ss are the duals of (Ker u_2'')_ss and (Coker u_2'')_ss, where u_2'' is the Poincaré-dual (transpose) map.
(2) Lemma: for X proper over k, the edge map H^i_DR(X) -> H^i(X,O_X) is an isomorphism on semisimple parts. Proof via the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence E_1^{a,b} = H^b(Ω^a) => H_DR. The absolute Frobenius acts p-linearly on the filtered de Rham complex, and it kills Ω^a for a ≥ 1 because F^*(f dg) = f^p d(g^p) = 0. Hence all E_1^{a,b} with a ≠ 0 have zero semisimple part. Since d_r is Frobenius-equivariant, the semisimple part of E_1^{0,b} consists of permanent cycles. Exactness of ( )_ss then gives (H^i_DR)_ss ≅ (E_∞^{0,i})_ss = (E_1^{0,i})_ss = H^i(O_X)_ss.
(3) He plans to rewrite u_2'' by Poincaré duality (struck out, flagged 'oubli dans 8.3', with a marginal corollary pointer). He then states 'Théorème' 8.5, completed on the next page. Assuming the crystalline formalism with torsion, there is an exact sequence
0 -> Ker v -> (pTors^n_cris(X))_ss -> (E(Y)⊗_W k)_ss -> Coker v -> 0,
where v : H^{n-1}(X,O_X)_ss -> H^{n-1}(Y,O_Y)_ss is restriction, so Coker v is the coherent vanishing cohomology.

Purpose: count the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius on the vanishing cohomology of Y that are p-adic units. Over a finite field this count is dim (E(Y)⊗k)_ss, because E(Y) is W-free. The theorem expresses it as the stable rank of the Hasse–Witt operator on the coherent vanishing cohomology, plus a nonnegative correction from p-torsion in H^n_cris(X). This is a torsion-corrected version of the Hasse–Witt / unit-root count that Katz proved for hypersurfaces (SGA 7 XXII), which the next page's margin mentions.

In modern terms, (H^i(O_X))_ss ≅ H^i_et(X_k̄, F_p)⊗k, and the slope-0 part of crystalline cohomology is H^i_et(X_k̄, Z_p)⊗W (Bloch–Illusie, de Rham–Witt). The sequence then amounts to universal coefficients for étale Z_p-cohomology of the pair (Y, X), with the ambient torsion entering the correction term.
errors: No mathematical error in the lemma. Its proof needs only that absolute Frobenius acts p-linearly on the de Rham complex compatibly with the stupid filtration, and that ( )_ss is exact. Properness is used only for finite-dimensionality.

The theorem is explicitly conditional ('En admettant les ingrédients...'). It assumes universal coefficients, Poincaré duality and weak Lefschetz for crystalline cohomology including torsion, which were not available when written. Weak Lefschetz with torsion for crystalline cohomology is subtle; Berthelot and later Illusie's de Rham–Witt supply the needed facts.

The duality claim for (Coker u_2)_ss and (Ker u_2)_ss requires u_2'' to be the transpose of u_2 under Poincaré duality. The author himself notes this was forgotten in 8.3 ('oubli dans 8.3 !') and struck the passage.

ideas.what: Equivalence between finite-dimensional k-spaces with bijective p-linear Frobenius and F_p-representations of Gal(k̄/k), with duality
ideas.modern_name: Lang's theorem / Katz's equivalence for unit-root (étale) φ-modules mod p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lang; Katz (SGA 7 XXII; 'p-adic properties of modular schemes', 1973)
ideas.where_published: Classical (Dieudonné/Lang); used in SGA 7 XXII by Katz

ideas.what: Semisimple (stable) part of de Rham cohomology equals semisimple part of H^i(X,O_X), proved via the Hodge spectral sequence and vanishing of Frobenius on Ω^{≥1}
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root / slope-0 part of de Rham cohomology; H^i(O_X)_ss ≅ H^i_et(X̄,F_p)⊗k
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Artin–Schreier, Serre (1958 Mexico paper), Katz SGA 7 XXII, Illusie (de Rham–Witt)

ideas.what: Exact sequence relating unit-root vanishing crystalline cohomology of a hypersurface section to the stable Hasse–Witt rank on coherent vanishing cohomology, corrected by p-torsion in H^n_cris(X)
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root count = stable rank of Hasse–Witt (Katz congruence formula), with torsion correction; étale Z_p universal coefficients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (SGA 7 XXII, 1973) for hypersurfaces in P^n; Bloch–Illusie for the slope-0 / étale Z_p comparison
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as known

missed.claim: An early, explicitly torsion-sensitive formulation of the unit-root/Hasse–Witt count for vanishing cohomology of a hypersurface section of an arbitrary smooth projective X. The correction term is the semisimple part of p-torsion in H^n_cris(X), together with Ker v. Katz's published version treats hypersurfaces in projective space, where no torsion occurs. The general torsion-corrected statement follows from later de Rham–Witt theory, but is rarely stated in this vanishing-cohomology form.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck anticipating the role of crystalline torsion in Hasse–Witt / Newton-polygon questions before Illusie's de Rham–Witt complex. The mathematics is recoverable today via étale Z_p-cohomology.

deep.surprise_reason: The lemma is folklore and the semisimple-linear-algebra/duality is classical. The theorem is a conditional, torsion-aware variant of Katz's unit-root count, which is now essentially a consequence of de Rham–Witt theory and étale Z_p universal coefficients. It is historically interesting as early crystalline-torsion thinking, but not a missed result.
